title: Continuity-aware KV-prefix batchbench for mixed-traffic p95 and tokens/sec regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible microbenchmark harness that measures how continuous batching interacts with queueing when multiple tenant profiles (short chat, long completions, embeddings) share the same runtime. Focus on p95 latency shifts and tokens/sec throughput regressions that only become visible under continuity (persistent KV cache) and realistic prefix reuse patterns.
background: Previous probes focused on burst/microburst and stratified arrivals but often omitted realistic KV prefix reuse and continuity across sessions. In production, we see long-running sessions that maintain warmed KV caches and shorter requests that benefit from prefix collapse; this changes batching behavior and queue dynamics. We need a harness that reproduces this continuity, isolates kernel scheduling effects, and surfaces regressions in p95 tokens/sec under controlled model/kernel variants.
objective: 1) Build an automated benchmark that simulates continuous sessions with KV-prefix reuse alongside stateless short requests. 2) Quantify p95 latency and tokens/sec surface across arrival mixes and batching parameters. 3) Implement automated regression detection and alerting tied to CI and nightly runs.
success_metrics: Primary: clear separation of p95 latency and tokens/sec baselines for each workload mix (baseline vs candidate) with statistical significance (95% CI). Secondary: regression detector flags true positives <5% false positive rate on historical runs, run-to-run variance under 3% for tokens/sec at median load.
harness_config:
- Harness name: continuity-kv-prefix-batchbench
- Engine hooks: runtime-instrumentation for per-request batch_id, kv_hit boolean, kernel_variant tag
- Measurement window: 30-minute steady-state after 5-minute warmup
- Aggregation: 1s microbins, derive p50/p90/p95/p99 for latency and tokens/sec, plus tail-sampling traces for slow requests
- Output: CSV time-series, Grafana dashboard snapshots, annotated run artifact in CI
workload_profiles: Profile A (long-session): 10% of sessions, avg 1200 tokens req, high KV locality (80% prefix reuse), arrival rate low but persistent. Profile B (short burst): 70% of requests, 20-80 tokens, low KV reuse, Poisson arrivals. Profile C (embeddings): 20% of requests, stateless, CPU-bound pre/post processing. Mixes to test: 90/10 short/long, 70/20/10 (short/long/embeddings), bimodal 50/50.
arrival_distributions:
- Long sessions: periodic arrivals following a renewal process with session stickiness (inter-arrival mean 10s, CV=1.2)
- Short requests: Poisson with configurable lambda to hit target TPS
- Embeddings: bursty with on-off Pareto model to stress queue backpressure
batching_and_queue_policies:
- Continuous batching enabled with batch_age cap options: [5ms, 10ms, 25ms]
- Batch size cap: [8, 16, 32]
- Queueing discipline: FIFO baseline, experiment with priority tagging for long-session affinity to measure priority inversion effects
- KV-aware routing: enable/disable routing warm sessions to dedicated pool
instrumentation:
- Collect per-request: start_ts, end_ts, tokens_generated, batch_size, kv_hit, kernel_variant, cpu_gpu_util, pod_id
- Derive tokens/sec by summing tokens_generated across microbins divided by time
- Compute p95 latencies per workload class and combined
- Tail traces: capture stack/kernels for top 1% slowest requests
regression_detection:
- Baseline: nightly median-run for each mix stored with time-series snapshot.
- Detector: two-sided paired t-test on p95 across 20 independent trials (or non-parametric bootstrap if distributions non-normal).
- Thresholds: absolute p95 increase >10% and tokens/sec drop >7% flagged as regression.
- CI integration: failing candidate build posts GitHub PR comment with link to dashboard and CSV artifact
analysis_plan: 1) Run factorial experiments across batch_age x batch_size x mix to build surface maps. 2) For candidate kernel/model changes compare surfaces to baseline and compute iso-lines where p95 crosses SLO thresholds. 3) Use heatmap visualization of tokens/sec delta and p95 delta; highlight kernel-config pairs that cause >10% p95 regression. 4) For flagged regressions run targeted debug: enable detailed tracing and CPU/GPU timelines and collect kernel occupancy metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness reproducibly runs in CI and produces artifacts within 45 minutes per full sweep.
- Detector runs and produces a deterministic pass/fail decision for known synthetic regressions injected by perturbing batching delay.
- Dashboard templates for ops and eng with linked traces are generated automatically.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: harness noise from multi-tenant infra. Mitigation: run on isolated dedicated pool and repeat runs to reduce variance.
- Risk: long warmup time for KV caches. Mitigation: pre-warm sessions and use snapshot restore where possible.
- Risk: detector false positives. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and require manual triage on borderline alerts.
next_steps: 1) Merge harness scaffolding PR and schedule nightly run (Benji). 2) Add kernel_variant tagging to runtime instrumentation (Claire). 3) Run first full-factorial sweep and upload baseline (Aisha). 4) Wire detector to CI and add PR comment integration.
